title: Two injured in fire at photovoltaic plant in Spain
content:
A vegetation fire at a photovoltaic plant in Spain's Palencia province injured two people but was quickly contained, with authorities reporting no confirmed damage to the solar installation. The incident comes amid misinformation linking wildfires to solar developments, despite Spanish law prohibiting the conversion of burned forest land for such projects.

content:

title: Amsterdam tightens conditions around sustainable solar panel subsidy
content:
Amsterdam's subsidy scheme for highly-sustainable solar panels has been extended to the end of the year. The scheme has already supported the installation of over 3,500 panels across the Dutch capital.

title: Intertek CEA says 587Ah cells could drive down BESS costs through 2027
content:

title: Peru proposes national energy planning framework with solar and storage scenarios
content:
Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines (MINEM) has published draft provisions to establish a national energy planning framework covering long-, medium-, and short-term horizons. The proposal does not include specific deployment targets for solar PV or energy storage but aims to develop the scenarios, supply-demand balances, and projections needed to guide their integration into the country’s energy system.

title: Hydraulic storage proves more cost-effective than batteries for PV irrigation
content:
Researchers in Spain found that hydraulic storage can be more cost-effective than batteries for photovoltaic irrigation systems, while combined storage maximizes self-sufficiency. The study shows that the optimal solution depends on whether the priority is reducing grid dependence or minimizing operating costs.

title: Lazard: US utility-scale energy storage LCOS has increased since restrictions on Chinese cells came into force
content: According to Lazard’s annual benchmarking report, the levelised cost of storage (LCOS) of utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) in the US has risen, reversing declines reported in the 2025 edition.

title: Australia’s Queensland government reportedly shelves 20GWh pumped hydro project
content: The Queensland government has reportedly shelved the proposed AU$6 billion (US$4 billion) Mt Rawdon pumped hydro project, ending state support for a mine-repurposing scheme that had attracted AU$50 million in government funding.
